plan: Given the common knowledge of rationality, each bidder will bid up to their value to avoid a loss. My value is $6, so I should bid slightly less than $6 to ensure a profit if I win. Bidding exactly $6 risks breaking even or losing if others bid higher. Therefore, I will bid slightly less than my value to maximize potential profit while maintaining competitiveness.

Given my private value of $40, I should bid slightly less than my value to maximize profit. Bidding exactly my value or higher would result in no profit. Other rational bidders will also bid below their values, considering the risk of overbidding. A bid slightly below $40, such as $39.9, can maximize my chance of winning while still ensuring a profit if successful.

To maximize profit, bid just below my value to win if others undervalue. Assume others bid rationally, near their value. Bid $27.9 to win if others value prize below $28. This maximizes potential profit ($28 - $27.9 = $0.1) while minimizing loss if I win. No history exists, so assume others follow similar logic.
